IMG_1061.HEIC.historical_summary: This document is a Sharia court record or a legal deed, dated 20 Recep 1330 Hijri (approximately January 10, 1912 Gregorian), concerning a property transaction or dispute in Izmir. The document's heading indicates it pertains to 'Abuzur' and bears a stamp duty value of ten kuruş, with an affixed 5 kuruş Ottoman revenue stamp from 1330 Hijri. The core of the document details a property located in the Karataş, Şehid, and Vandoniye quarters of Izmir. A key party involved is Espina, identified as a woman of the Greek nation from Kayseri, daughter of Pavli Apostoloğlu. The 'Ottoman Rolandiye Bank' is also mentioned, suggesting its involvement, possibly as a previous owner, mortgagee, or a party to the transaction. The document repeatedly refers to the property as having a 'foreign number' (nümara-i garibe) and mentions a transfer deed (tahviliye) originating 'from three hundred women of the nation' (üç yüz milletli nisvanından). This unusual phrase might indicate a collective ownership, a specific type of trust, or a large group of beneficiaries, potentially linked to the bank or a community. The proceedings took place in the Sharia Court of the Enver Sharia Council, specifically in the legal section of the Court of Appeals, where an official named İsmet was present, and a declaration was made by an unnamed person. The document serves as a record of this declaration or a deed issued as a result of the court's decision regarding the property's status or transfer.

IMG_1062.HEIC.historical_summary: This document is an Ottoman land title deed (Tapu Senedi) issued by the General Directorate of Land Registry and Cadastre. It formally records the full ownership of a specific property, consisting of a house and an adjacent plot of land. The property is situated in the Aşağı Mahalle (Lower Quarter) of Çerkezköy village, which falls under the Saray Nahiye, Vize Kaza, Kırkkilise Sanjak, and Edirne Vilayet. The deed identifies the joint owners as Mehmed bin Ali and his wife Fatma bint-i Hüseyin, both residents of Çerkezköy, each holding a half share of the property. The document meticulously details the property's boundaries, specifying a road to the north and the houses of Mustafa Efendi, Mehmed Efendi, and Ahmed Efendi to the south, east, and west, respectively. This official record, dated 20 Shawwal 1320 Hijri (January 19, 1903 Gregorian), served to legally confirm and protect the owners' rights to the land and structure.
